basics.name: Jianshu Wang
basics.label: Research Assistant | Applied Psychology
basics.summary: Applied psychology graduate combining behavioral experiments, EEG/ERP analysis, and computational behavioral modeling in cognitive neuroscience and human-computer interaction.

work.name: Minzu University of China
work.summary: Supervisor: Dr. Ze Geng. EEG analysis and behavioral modeling.
highlights: Preprocess EEG recordings and extract single-trial centroparietal positivity (CPP) slopes to characterize neural evidence accumulation.
Fit drift diffusion models to IAT response times and accuracy using PyDDM, comparing model specifications with BIC.
Integrate trial-level neural measures with behavioral decision models; completed all data analyses for a manuscript submitted to the Journal of Environmental Psychology.

work.name: Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences (ISCAS)
work.summary: Supervisors: Dr. Chao Zhou and Prof. Jin Huang. Human performance during whole-body motion.
highlights: Developed Unity-based directional-judgment experiments on a 6-DOF motion platform.
Analyzed response times in relation to task-relative motion components and individual differences; contributed to a manuscript submitted to CHI 2027.

work.name: Human Factors in Driving Takeover
highlights: Independently developed a Unity-based VR driving scenario using PICO 4 Pro, integrating eye tracking with ECG, GSR, and EMG recording.
Designed a two-stage warning experiment examining cognitive load and the monitoring-to-takeover request interval in situation-awareness recovery and takeover performance.
Analyzed behavioral and physiological data alongside individual differences in personality and driving style.

work.name: Shenzhen University
work.summary: Supervisor: Prof. Zhenhong He. Loss and compensation in decision-making.
highlights: Designed experiments and programmed behavioral tasks in PsychoPy for research on loss and compensatory decisions.
Developed Python data-analysis pipelines and applied drift diffusion and reinforcement-learning models to behavioral data.

work.name: Human-AI Ethics
highlights: Designed and programmed PsychoPy experiments examining how AI supervision and incentives influence dishonest behavior and ethical decision-making.
Analyzed behavioral data in Python/R using mixed-effects models; co-first author of the resulting Acta Psychologica Sinica article.
Selected coursework: Psychological Statistics, Experimental Psychology, Cognitive Psychology, Advanced Psychology Research Methods
